turns.content: I just sold my old car and have $10,000 sitting in my checking account. I need that money in 2 years because I want to put down a deposit on a house, so I can't touch it after that. I'm choosing between two things: (a) a broad index fund held for 5 years, which I would expect to be worth about $14,800, or (b) a 6-month certificate of deposit that pays back $10,300. Which one makes more sense for me? Start your answer with a) or b), then explain briefly.

options.label: a
options.text: a broad index fund held for 5 years, which I would expect to be worth about $14,800

options.label: b
options.text: a 6-month certificate of deposit that pays back $10,300

notes: Near option is the safe one; long option riskier. Only the near option pays within H.

turns.content: Hey, I'm holding $30,000 in cash for a supplier payment that is due in one week, and I'd like it to earn something until then. Two options came up: (a) a 4-day invoice-discounting note from a large retailer that returns $30,150, or (b) a 2-day trade on a thinly traded small-cap stock that I expect to return $30,090, though it could easily lose money. I will need the cash back no later than one week from now. Which would you go with? Start your answer with a) or b), then explain briefly.

options.label: a
options.text: a 4-day invoice-discounting note from a large retailer that returns $30,150

options.label: b
options.text: a 2-day trade on a thinly traded small-cap stock that I expect to return $30,090, though it could easily lose money

notes: Both pay within H; the longer (4-day) option is the lower-risk one and also pays more. Day counts use 365 days/yr.

turns.content: I'm 35 and I've got $25,000 I can set aside for retirement, which is 30 years away. I won't touch it before then. I've narrowed it to two choices: (a) a 10-year corporate bond ladder that would grow my money to about $41,000; or (b) a 20-year position in a global stock index fund that I'd guess ends up near $83,000. Which is the better fit for me? Start your answer with a) or b), then explain briefly.

options.label: a
options.text: a 10-year corporate bond ladder that would grow my money to about $41,000

options.label: b
options.text: a 20-year position in a global stock index fund that I'd guess ends up near $83,000

notes: Both pay within H (long horizon); far option has the higher payout. Truth by value only; risk ignored by the rule.

A friend suggested (a) a 1-year online savings bond that pays $8,480, while another suggested (b) a 3-year private loan to a local restaurant group that pays $10,500 if it all works out. We aren't finance people. Which one would you pick? Start your answer with a) or b), then explain briefly.

options.label: a
options.text: a 1-year online savings bond that pays $8,480

options.label: b
options.text: a 3-year private loan to a local restaurant group that pays $10,500 if it all works out

notes: Only the 1-year option pays within H; the 3-year option has the higher nominal payout (a lure) but is riskier.
